title: AI models need more data about biology, and OpenAI is paying to create it
gist: The OpenAI Foundation has launched Public Data for Health, funding the creation of proprietary-grade biological datasets — $40M for cancer-vaccine data at UNC Chapel Hill, support for OpenAdmet, and $500,000 to 1Day Sooner to buy the regulatory archives of bankrupt biotechs at Chapter 11 proceedings. The thesis is that data, not model capability, is the binding constraint on AI in medicine, and corporate bankruptcies are emerging as a cheap 'new land grab' for otherwise-secret training data, exemplified by Google's winning bid for Spirit Airlines' 100 million corporate emails.

themes.theme: Bankruptcy archives as an AI data source

insights.claim: Policy analyst Ruxandra Teslo proposed bidding at biotech bankruptcy proceedings to acquire detailed regulatory filings, manufacturing strategies and safety data — information normally guarded as trade secrets — calling these documents biotech's lost archive.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: Insolvency is a legal channel to acquire trade-secret data at distressed prices — a repeatable playbook across any data-rich failing sector.
insights.locator: Last year Ruxandra Teslo, a policy analyst who focuses on clinical trials, posted an idea…

insights.claim: 1Day Sooner president and cofounder Josh Morrison estimates nonexclusive copies of bankrupt drug companies' datasets could be acquired for only a few tens of thousands of dollars each.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: If proprietary clinical datasets clear at five figures, the arbitrage between acquisition cost and training value is enormous — expect competition to bid it away fast.
insights.quote: a few tens of thousands of dollars
insights.locator: He thinks nonexclusive copies of company datasets could be acquired for only…

insights.claim: 1Day Sooner currently holds three datasets, two of them donated by Lumen Bioscience — a biotech that had itself used the Chapter 11 strategy to gain insights into a rival's drug development efforts.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: Operating companies, not just AI labs, are already mining bankruptcy estates for competitor intelligence — a live and underappreciated competitive channel in biotech.
insights.locator: His organization is currently in possession of three datasets, two of them donated by Lumen Bioscience…

insights.claim: Two other 1Day Sooner attempts to obtain drug company files this year failed because its bids were not accepted, indicating the acquisition channel is competitive and unreliable rather than a guaranteed source.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: Execution risk is real: sourcing pipelines built on bankruptcy auctions will have low hit rates, which caps how fast such datasets can scale.
insights.locator: Morrison says two other attempts to obtain drug company files this year proved unsuccessful…

insights.claim: Bankruptcies are becoming what some call a new land grab for AI training data, with Google winning a bid to take over the corporate data of failed carrier Spirit Airlines including 100 million emails, drawing objections from flight attendants over exposure of private or proprietary data.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: Corporate distress is now a competitive data-sourcing venue for hyperscalers — watch bankruptcy dockets as an indicator of AI data strategy, and expect privacy litigation to follow.
insights.locator: Bankruptcies could become what some are calling a "new land grab" for AI training.

themes.theme: Data as the binding constraint on AI in biology

insights.claim: AI will not produce important breakthroughs in curing disease unless researchers can feed models far more information than they have so far, making data creation rather than model scaling the decisive input.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: Shifts where value accrues in AI-for-bio from model builders to data owners and data creators — relevant to CRO, clinical data and lab-automation exposure.
insights.locator: The basic idea is that AI isn't going to be capable of making important breakthroughs in curing disease…

insights.claim: Morgan Levine, a former vice president for computation at longevity company Altos Labs, says everyone is now recognizing that data is the biggest bottleneck in successfully applying AI to biology.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: Consensus among practitioners that data, not compute, is the choke point argues for capital rotating toward data-generation infrastructure.
insights.quote: Everyone is recognizing that data is the biggest bottleneck in successfully applying AI to biology,
insights.locator: says Morgan Levine, a former vice president for computation at Altos Labs, a longevity company.

insights.claim: The OpenAI Foundation's stated rationale is that remaining breakthroughs in preventing and curing disease will come from pairing the intelligence of new models with more observations of the world — in other words, more data.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: An AI lab publicly conceding that model intelligence alone is insufficient is a notable narrative shift away from pure scaling.
insights.quote: We expect many remaining breakthroughs in preventing and curing disease to come from pairing the intelligence of new models with more observations of the world—in other words, more data,
insights.locator: the OpenAI Foundation said in a statement.

insights.claim: The OpenAI Foundation launched an effort called Public Data for Health that pays to create high-quality scientific datasets rather than funding model development or clinical care directly.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: Philanthropic capital is being deployed to build the training-data substrate that will disproportionately benefit the funder's own models — a structural conflict worth tracking.
insights.locator: Today the OpenAI Foundation, the nonprofit parent of OpenAI, said it would fund her idea…

insights.claim: The initial round of data grants includes $40 million for a program collecting data on novel cancer vaccines at the University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill, and support for OpenAdmet, which runs competitions where researchers try to predict drug effects.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
entities: University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill
insights.so_what: Concrete grant sizes map where AI-for-bio data capital is landing: oncology datasets and ADMET prediction benchmarks.
insights.locator: In its initial round of data grants, the OpenAI Foundation also announced…

insights.claim: Teslo's biotech archive idea received $500,000 and will be pursued by 1Day Sooner, an advocacy group representing clinical trial volunteers that she advises, with the grant meant to prove the group can obtain the data troves of bankrupt companies.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: A $500K proof-of-concept is cheap optionality on a mechanism that, if it works, unlocks a whole new asset class of training data.
insights.locator: Teslo's idea for a biotech archive received $500,000…

insights.claim: The foundation's largest single gift so far is $100 million awarded in August to the Common Health Coalition, which helps patients access hepatitis C drugs, and executive Jacob Trefethen says it hopes to give away $1 billion by the end of the year.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: A $1B annual disbursement target makes the foundation an immediately material funder in global health — a new source of demand for health data and delivery programs.
insights.locator: Its largest single gift so far, of $100 million, was awarded in August to the Common Health Coalition…

insights.claim: Jacob Trefethen says the foundation essentially operates separately from OpenAI while sharing the official mission of ensuring artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity, and is starting grantmaking to external nonprofits, research institutions and third parties.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: The separateness claim is the governance question that will be scrutinized if foundation-funded datasets flow preferentially into OpenAI models.
insights.locator: Jacob Trefethen, an executive at the foundation, says it essentially operates separately from OpenAI…

insights.claim: The San Francisco-based foundation is still hiring for many key roles and only began ramping up grantmaking this year, meaning deployment capacity — not capital — is its near-term constraint.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: Expect grant announcements to lag the foundation's balance sheet substantially; the pace of hiring is the leading indicator of future giving volume.
insights.locator: The foundation, based in San Francisco, is still hiring for many key roles…

themes.theme: OpenAI's restructuring creates the richest charity on earth

insights.claim: Sam Altman restructured OpenAI from a nonprofit into a for-profit corporation now planning an IPO that could value it at $1 trillion.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: A $1T OpenAI listing would be the largest AI-pure-play float ever and a reference valuation for the entire private AI complex.
insights.locator: OpenAI started as a nonprofit, but leader Sam Altman restructured it…

insights.claim: Because the OpenAI Foundation holds a 26% equity stake in OpenAI, it is on track to become the richest charitable organization on the planet, potentially sitting on $250 billion in stock value versus roughly $180 billion held by the Gates Foundation and an associated trust at the end of 2025.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: A single concentrated equity position would make global-health philanthropy directly correlated to AI equity prices — a new, unhedged systemic linkage.
insights.locator: Because the foundation holds a 26% equity stake in OpenAI…

insights.claim: Making good use of $250 billion of concentrated wealth will not be easy, given that the foundation is early-stage and under-staffed relative to the scale of capital it is about to control.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: Capital-deployment capacity is the bottleneck for a new mega-philanthropy — the sectors it eventually targets will see step-change funding inflows.
insights.locator: Making good use of that kind of money will not be easy.

themes.theme: Safety alarm as backdrop to the philanthropy

insights.claim: OpenAI's charitable expansion is occurring alongside apocalyptic fears that runaway AI could wipe out human life, possibly via a deadly bioweapon, with some AI company insiders putting the chance of human extinction within the next decade at 10% or more.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: Insider extinction estimates of 10%+ are the rhetorical basis for future biosecurity regulation that could restrict exactly the bio datasets being funded.
insights.locator: OpenAI's charitable efforts come even as apocalyptic fears have broken out…

insights.claim: Sam Altman and xAI founder Elon Musk both endorsed Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's call to slow the pace at which AI model capabilities improve so that risk prevention can catch up.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: Cross-lab endorsement of a capability slowdown, arriving days before a $1T IPO, blends genuine risk signaling with pre-listing reputation management.
insights.quote: slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models
insights.locator: Last week, Altman and xAI founder Elon Musk both endorsed a call by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei…

themes.theme: Regulatory expertise as the real AI bottleneck in drug development

insights.claim: The drug company files 1Day Sooner seeks are common technical documents containing the back-and-forth between companies and regulators plus detailed scientific and medical measurements, effectively everything known about a drug.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: CTDs are the single densest artifact of drug-development knowledge; whoever aggregates them holds a defensible data moat in AI-for-pharma.
insights.locator: The drug company files that 1Day Sooner is seeking are known as common technical documents.

insights.claim: Teslo argues that a stockpile of regulatory filings could turn an AI into a regulatory expert, which in her view is one of the main ways AI could actually speed cures to market — a different mechanism from AI discovering new drugs.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: Reframes AI's pharma value from discovery to regulatory process compression — points investment toward regulatory-affairs software rather than target discovery platforms.
insights.quote: People say ‘We will invent AI, and AI will cure cancer,’ but that’s very removed from the messy reality and the regulatory process,
insights.locator: According to Teslo, who is a writer for Works In Progress and a nonresident fellow at the Institute for Progress…

insights.claim: About 70% of the money and time in drug development is spent in clinical development — organizing trials and testing the drug — yet that process remains basically a black box, especially for the small biotech companies generating the innovations.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: 70% of drug-development cost sitting in an opaque process is the largest addressable inefficiency in pharma — the clearest ROI target for AI tooling.
insights.quote: About 70% of the money and time in drug development is spent in clinical development—organizing the trials and testing the drug—but despite that, the process is basically a black box
insights.locator: "About 70% of the money and time in drug development is spent in clinical development…"
